facts.text: Imam Muhammad bin Saud founded the First Saudi State in 1727. Diriyah was its capital; Salwa Palace in At-Turaif was a seat of government.
The First Saudi State ended in 1818 after Ibrahim Pasha's campaign took Diriyah. Its rulers included Muhammad bin Saud, Abdulaziz bin Muhammad, Saud bin Abdulaziz and Abdullah bin Saud.
Its establishment involved bringing previously fragmented areas under a common political authority. Avoid inventing particular motives, battles or treaties not in these notes.

facts.text: Turki bin Abdullah restored Saudi rule and founded the Second Saudi State in 1824 after recovering Riyadh and expelling Ottoman garrisons. Riyadh became its capital rather than Diriyah, which had been destroyed in the earlier campaign.
The Second Saudi State lasted until 1891. Its rulers included Turki bin Abdullah, Faisal bin Turki, Abdullah bin Faisal and Abdulrahman bin Faisal.
Distinguish restoration of rule, choice of capital, and the later establishment of the present kingdom; these are different events.

facts.text: Ibn al-Haytham, also called Alhazen, lived from 965 to 1040. He worked in mathematics, physics and astronomy and moved from Basra to Cairo.
His Book of Optics studied light using mathematical analysis and experiments. He designed experiments to test hypotheses rather than treating inherited authorities as sufficient proof.

UNESCO celebrated him as a pioneer of optics during the International Year of Light in 2015. He investigated reflection, refraction and how light travels. Do not claim he invented every later optical device or science itself.

facts.text: A light-year measures the distance light travels in one year, approximately 9.46 trillion kilometres.
Light travels through space at approximately 300,000 kilometres per second. Large distances therefore still take time to cross.
Earth is approximately eight light-minutes from the Sun.
